text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Multiple serving-runtime pods in pool-gpu-3 are restarting. Observed symptoms: repeated OOMs followed by CUDA illegal memory access in the container logs. Auto-escalating to on-call.

nate.h: saw the alert, looking. Pods 3/7 in pool-gpu-3 restarted in the last 2 minutes. kube events show OOMKilled -> CrashLoopBackOff for two replicas. Attaching recent container log tail:

nate.h:
```
...
2026-03-15T18:42:10Z ERROR runtime: cuda illegal memory access at 0x7ffdeadbeef
2026-03-15T18:42:10Z INFO model-serving: falling back to standby model
2026-03-15T18:42:11Z FATAL oom: killed process 1278 (model_worker)
...
```

sara.p: interesting — kernel dmesg from node gpu-node-17 shows pagewalk faults and SMMU messages right before the container OOM: `nv: illegal device address 0x... pagewalk failure`. Could be a driver/kernel interaction or model hitting a corner-case with KV cache memory.

jamal: i'm attaching the kube describe + events for the node and pod (pastebin link): https://paste.redwood/gpu-node-17-events

ml-oncall: we saw elevated large-sequence requests from customer 'fast-chat' at ~18:41 UTC; they had a ramp of long-context requests which increases KV cache pressure. Could be correlated.

infra-eng: quick triage checklist —
- cordon gpu-node-17
- drain non-critical pods
- scale up pool-gpu-3 by +1 node if capacity allows
- enable fallback policy to cpu-quantized for the slow path

sara.p: cordoning node now: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17` (done). Draining non-prod pods: starting.

nate.h: scaling pool-gpu-3 up via infra autoscaler request — submitted a hot add: +1 (request id 0x7c9). If autoscaler fails, fallback to routing lower tier models.

incident-bot: NOTE: routing policy applied: requests to model:redwood-llama-large now autoretry -> model:redwood-llama-medium on failure (applied by nate.h).

jamal: i pulled the kernel trace from node — stack shows repeated unaligned deviceaddr in NV kernel module, then driver crash, then userland sees illegal memory access. Snippet:

jamal:
```
[ 3245.128412] nv 0000:3a:00.0: device addr walk failed, status 0x2
[ 3245.128420] WARNING: CPU: 1 PID: 1023 at /drivers/nvidia/mm/smmu.c:line 421
[ 3245.128431] BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference in nv_smmu_walk()
```

ml-oncall: given the stack, this looks like a possible SMMU corner-case in combination with our allocator pattern. Repro steps being prepared. We may need to temporarily disable driver prefetch or reduce max KV cache size as mitigation.

sara.p: customer-impact check: `fast-chat` reports ~12% error rate on their traffic (ingress metrics). Other customers in pool-gpu-3 show <1% except one more small customer whose heavy batches started at the same time.

nate.h: mitigation plan executed so far:
- cordon gpu-node-17 (done)
- drained non-prod pods (done)
- applied routing fallback to medium model (done)
- requested +1 node to pool (pending)
- set autoscaler emergency threshold to avoid further pack scheduling on that node

infra-eng: we should also pin the nodes to a previous driver version if the new driver triggered this. Checking driver rollout history... driver v525 was rolled last night to a subset of GPU nodes. gpu-node-17 is on v525.

jamal: reproducer notes: long context (>=16k) + large batch sizes + concurrent KV writes triggers the sequence quickly. I'll open a kernel-driver bug with the stack and link here once created.

incident-bot: customer-notify-bot triggered: DRAFT:
```
To: fast-chat SRE
Subject: Brief outage: degraded service for inference on pool-gpu-3
Body: We observed transient errors and elevated latencies between 18:40–18:46 UTC due to GPU node instability. We have cordoned the affected node, routed traffic to alternate models and are adding capacity. Root cause investigation ongoing. We will update within 60 minutes.
```

customer-notify-bot: NOTIFICATION SENT to fast-chat (channel id: C0FFEE). (reaction :mailbox_with_mail:)

sara.p: autoscaler updated and new node is provisioning (cloud request id: req-903). If it comes up we should drain and repro on a sandbox node rather than force upgrades in prod.

nate.h: next steps for immediate mitigation:
1) keep node cordoned and evicted of serving pods
2) continue routing fallback and reduce per-request max KV cache to 50% for medium model
3) request kernel/driver team escalation with the collected dmesg + oops + reproducer
4) if new node not available within 10m, consider temporary cluster-wide throttle for long-seq requests to prevent KV pressure surge

jamal: created bug #RWI-7238 in kernel-driver board, linked logs and stack, assigned to driver-team oncall. url: https://tracker.redwood/RWI-7238

ml-oncall: quick mitigation implemented to reduce max KV per-session: `MODEL_KV_MAX=48` applied via feature-flag to pool-gpu-3 (rollout 5%). Monitoring error rate.

incident-bot: automation: rollback suggestion available — if errors persist after capacity + KV cap, consider rolling back driver v525 to v520 for subset of GPU fleet.

sara.p: error rate dropped to 1.8% after KV cap + routing fallback. Latency normalized for most customers. Still keeping node cordoned until kernel-team confirms.

nate.h: preparing handoff to night on-call (jamal) at 19:00 UTC. Summary for handoff:
- incident id: 2026-03-15-gpu-illegal-4299001234
- root symptom: cuda illegal mem access and OOMs on gpu-node-17 during high KV pressure
- mitigations: node cordoned/drained, routing fallback applied, KV cap feature-flag applied, +1 node requested (pending)
- open actions: driver-team triage on RWI-7238, monitor error rates and autoscaler
- customer impact: fast-chat ~12% errors for ~6 minutes, reduced to ~1.8% after mitigations; monitoring will continue.

jamal: acknowledged handoff. i'll take next watch and chase driver-team. i'll escalate to infra if autoscaler fails to add capacity within 10 minutes.

customer-notify-bot: UPDATE SENT to fast-chat: brief update with mitigation steps and ETA for next update in 30 minutes.

incident-bot: incident thread locked to maintain single-channel communication. If you need to add logs, append to the tracker RWI-7238; for customer comms use customer-notify-bot drafts.

nate.h: marking my oncall handoff note: `@jamal — all context in thread + tracker. ping me if you need kernel dumps or ephemeral repro infra.` (reaction :white_check_mark:)

jamal: will post follow-ups after driver-team responds and when the new node is up. Thanks all.
